findings.title: day_of_week normalization defeats stagger match
findings.problem: __create_cron_trigger normalizes day_of_week into expanded weekday names (line 711) before calling staggered_minute_hour (line 712). A crontab field that is semantically a full week but not written as a literal "*" (e.g. "0-7") normalizes into a comma-separated weekday list, so the stagger check's literal ("*", "*", "*") comparison no longer matches.
findings.impact: Datasources whose day_of_week field expresses a full week via a range rather than the literal "*" silently skip staggering even though they fire effectively daily, leaving the simultaneous-firing collision this change exists to prevent unaddressed for that cron shape.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate the raw (pre-normalization) day_of_week field against "*" when deciding whether to stagger, or pass the raw value into staggered_minute_hour instead of the APScheduler-normalized one. Whether other functionally-full-week spellings should also count is a scope call worth confirming explicitly rather than inferring from this review alone.

findings.title: hourly wildcard cron never staggered
findings.problem: staggered_minute_hour requires both minute and hour to be plain digit strings (line 73). Any cron with hour == "*" — the common hourly pattern, e.g. "0 * * * *" — fails the isdigit() check and is returned unchanged.
findings.impact: Datasources sharing an hourly cron still fire simultaneously every hour, reproducing the queue-timeout collision scenario this change targets, just on an hourly instead of daily cadence.
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly whether hour == "*" crons are in scope for staggering. If so, derive and apply a minute-only offset in that case; if not, this review cannot settle that on its own — confirm the exclusion is intentional rather than an unnoticed gap.
